runners_data.name: King's Crown
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has gone 2/15 on similar going without a win or place, making the Good surface a persistent concern; headgear (tongue-tie/pad) applied but the 27-day break and Sean Kirrane booking give little confidence in a race where the pace map works against deep closers.

runners_data.name: Curious Rover
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes the ride for a yard that has been quiet recently (0/8 over 14 days), but Curious Rover's 11/15 similar-going record including a win and three places makes him the most qualified hold-up runner in the field for conditions; must overcome a pace shape that is not genuinely searching.

runners_data.name: Brazen Idol
runners_data.note: Sean D Bowen partners this veteran hold-up type who has posted two seconds on Good ground recently, and the 11-day turnaround is not a concern given John Ryan's quick-fire approach; races from deep and needs the front two to tire, but on an honest-not-brutal tempo that looks unlikely.

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner with five wins from 13 starts at this track on Good ground, giving her a commanding course-and-conditions profile; Paul Mulrennan knows the horse well and she is ideally positioned to exploit an uncontested lead, though the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects this is still her preferred role rather than a forced tactical decision.

runners_data.name: Lion's House
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type whose natural finishing position is at the rear of the field — Connor Beasley gets the ride but the horse's 0W0P on similar going and a form string showing multiple double-figure finishes underscore the risk; repositioned to midfield on the map simply because the field is stacked with closers, not because his tactics will change.

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good ground (his only win), so the conditions suit, but William Pyle picks up an unfashionable booking and the recent form reads 8671 — this horse holds up naturally and, despite the map showing midfield, will likely settle further back than ideal with traffic to navigate.

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good ground here in August and has placed twice in similar company, giving him legitimate course credentials; Barry McHugh rides and the 33-day break is manageable, but as a genuine hold-up runner he needs more pace than Woohoo is likely to generate on her own.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Ran over 9f last time before reverting to 6f on Good — this 5f trip looks on the sharp side for a horse that has been campaigned at longer distances; Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim is useful but the style note is key — a natural hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map, not a natural 5f front-end performer.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with a 3/11 trainer strike over 14 days (Tristan Davidson in decent form), but this horse's 0W4P record at this level on similar going has never translated into a win; races from hold-up position and the 8-day turnaround is tight for a horse who finished 6th last time out.

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly who has never run on Good turf in Britain (1/5 on similar going), and dropping to 5f from 6f/7f is untested; headgear (hood) applied, David Allan is experienced, but the OR of 62 and poor going profile mean she faces a steep ask against older, course-savvy rivals.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's string is firing (6/53 over 14 days) and Wee Mary has a superb 8/15 similar-going record including a win and five places over this exact course and trip; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a tangible advantage, and as a genuine prominent type she is perfectly placed to make the most of tracking Woohoo's sustainable pace.

races.paceDynamic: Woohoo is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 5f Ayr handicap on Good ground, and with only Wee Mary lending any genuine prominent company, the early tempo is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than scorching. The pace map is significantly congested at the rear — Lion's House, Thistle Nil, Jm Jhingree, Hi Lord, Our Absent Friends, and Falcon Queen are all natural hold-up types but several are mapped to midfield simply because there is no room for them all to race from their true position, meaning the race shape at the back is considerably more compressed than it appears on paper. With Woohoo able to bowl along uncontested and set a measured gallop over this straight five furlongs on a sound surface, the race is likely to be run at an even, controlled tempo that rewards those who can travel prominently and produce a clean finishing kick without having to weave through traffic. This shape strongly favours the small band of genuine prominent racers — Woohoo herself and Wee Mary — who can sit close to the pace and sprint clear, while the large cluster of hold-up types face the dual problem of a non-searching tempo and no clear daylight to deliver their finishing effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Woohoo Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Woohoo sets a comfortable, uncontested pace and the tempo never truly tests the hold-up brigade.
scenarios.body: Woohoo dictates from the front at a gallop that suits her perfectly, with Wee Mary tracking closely and both able to sprint clear from the two-furlong pole without needing to find another gear from deep; the hold-up horses face a pace that is too honest but not too quick, leaving them short of the cover and gaps they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Wee Mary Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Wee Mary tracks Woohoo smoothly and produces a decisive late surge to reel her in close home.
scenarios.body: Wee Mary's strong recent form over this exact course and distance on Good ground — including a win and multiple places in this grade — positions her perfectly to sit on Woohoo's shoulder and pounce; Jim Goldie's yard is in excellent form (6/53 over 14 days) and Lauren Young's claim reduces the weight burden meaningfully.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just fast enough to stretch the field and create a gap for a hold-up runner to burst through on the stands' rail.
scenarios.body: Curious Rover has the best recent similar-going form figures of the hold-up runners (11/15 runs, 1W 3P on Good or similar) and Jason Hart is an experienced handler of these tactical situations; however, most rivals in this group are tagged as redistributed and are not true closers, limiting genuine candidates and making this scenario difficult to execute cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Two Fail
scenarios.trigger: If Woohoo and Wee Mary burn each other out fighting for control and both empty inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Should either horse push the other harder than anticipated, the even early gallop could tip into a pace that brings the mid-pack runners into play; Brazen Idol, who has twice finished second at this level on Good ground, and Hi Lord, a recent course winner, would be the main beneficiaries if the front two tire.

watchPoints.text: Woohoo's early position is the race's hinge point — if Paul Mulrennan is allowed to roll along uncontested in front, the whole field is racing to her tune and hold-up horses face a near-impossible task.
Wee Mary and Woohoo are both trained by Jim Goldie, raising the possibility of stable tactics being deployed — watch to see whether Wee Mary is asked to push Woohoo or is given a watching brief.

The cluster of six genuinely hold-up types (Lion's House, Jm Jhingree, Hi Lord, Thistle Nil, Our Absent Friends, Falcon Queen) all mapped to midfield will create significant traffic issues in the straight — watch for crowding on the stands' rail inside the final furlong.
Curious Rover's Jason Hart is a rider who excels at finding gaps on straight tracks — watch for him to angle away from the rail early to find clear air if the midfield bunches.

Hi Lord's strong course form (won here on Good in August) makes him the most credible hold-up threat if the pace quickens late — watch his position at the two-furlong marker to gauge whether he has any chance of closing.

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 4yo with a string of placed efforts over 5f on Good, stepping up to 6f here which may stretch her stamina slightly; Nigel Tinkler's runner is 17 days fresh and apprentice Alex Jary claims 3lb, which helps at the weights.

runners_data.name: Taygar
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's 5yo has been model of consistency at 6f on Good, with seven placed efforts from 14 runs on similar ground — he finds a way to be competitive without necessarily winning; Sean Kirrane takes the ride on a horse who will travel prominently throughout.

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 8yo is the race's lone pace-setter and will make all, but its STYLE_FIT flag signals it is performing outside its optimal role here — only 3 from 15 runs on similar Going suggest Good turf may not bring out the best; Paul Mulrennan knows the horse and will try to steal it on the front end.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Five-pound claimer Lauren Young partners this Jim Goldie 5yo, who has been placed in four of her last six starts at 5-6f on Good and is consistent enough to hit the frame if given a clear run; 39 days since her last run is worth noting but she has returned fresh before.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up performer who won over 6f on Good and placed at 7f — the step back to 6f at Ayr suits and Sean D Bowen is a strong booking; only 7 days since her last run and she handles Good ground well with six runs on similar conditions.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: A genuine closer whose recent form over 6-7f on softer or standard ground has been mixed, and she needs the pace to truly collapse to get involved from her hold-up position; David Allan rides and the horse's best effort on Good ground (3rd) came over 6f, which is at least a positive data point.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's 5yo is a genuine back-of-field performer by style but has been pushed into a midfield slot by the race's configuration — his best form shows on 5f or 6f on Good (2 wins from 12 on similar going), but racing forward of where he wants to be makes life harder; Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim is some compensation.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6yo won over 6f on Soft and has placed twice at 5f on Good, giving him course-relevant form credentials; he races in a visor and is a natural hold-up horse by style, though this race's configuration means he is mapped into midfield rather than off the pace where he does his best work.

runners_data.name: Wee Dresser
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's 3yo has shown modest but consistent form at 6f on Good, with a placing in her most recent run at that trip and distance suiting; Jason Hart is an experienced jockey but the horse's overall record (0 wins, 1 place from 3 runs on similar going) doesn't inspire confidence in this grade.

races.paceDynamic: Water Of Leith is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good ground at Ayr over 6f, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, unhurried clip without any genuine rival prepared to match strides from the front. Azuinthejungle and Taygar are both prominent-style horses who will sit close to the pace, but neither has the profile to force a genuine test, meaning Water Of Leith can dictate terms at a tempo that suits those travelling just off it. The field contains more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate naturally — Royal Duke and Doon The Glen are both genuine closers redistributed into midfield slots, meaning they are unlikely to get the truly patient, off-the-pace ride they prefer, which compromises their chance in this shape. A controlled, single-lead scenario over 6f on Good ground at Ayr strongly favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than late-closers who need a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith leads at a steady clip and the prominent pair press without forcing a strong pace.
scenarios.body: Water Of Leith dictates throughout at a comfortable tempo, setting up a race where horses racing just behind have the energy to quicken and challenge entering the final furlong; on Good Ayr ground over 6f this scenario rewards those who travel smoothly in the first three.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith sets a searingly fast early tempo and ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly strong pace would cause front-runners to stop in the straight, allowing the hold-up horses to pick up ground late; White Ladder and Wee Dresser, who genuinely travel off a fast pace, would be best placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses contest the early lead, creating a brief scrappy pace before a tactical reset.
scenarios.body: Azuinthejungle and Taygar both looking to sit close to Water Of Leith could create minor early crowding that disrupts rhythm, gifting a cleaner run to horses tucked in midfield who avoid trouble; Thunderstorm Katie's consistent placed form on Good ground makes her the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely end-to-end and horses finish tired, allowing the rearmost to mow through.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Doon The Glen and Royal Duke to secure their natural back-of-field position and produce sustained finishes, which this race shape makes structurally unlikely given they have been pushed forward by the field's configuration; their style-fit discounts reduce the probability markedly.

watchPoints.text: Watch Water Of Leith's early sectionals — if Paul Mulrennan is allowed to dictate a slow pace unchallenged, the horse's ability to steal this on the front end becomes a live danger despite the style-fit caveat.

Azuinthejungle and Taygar will both try to sit just off the leader and could briefly jostle for the same ground exiting the stalls — any interference or checked stride for either in the first furlong would compromise their chance in a 6f sprint.

Royal Duke and Doon The Glen are natural closers who may struggle to find their preferred position on the outer or rear in a small 9-runner field — if they are forced to race more prominently than ideal, their finishing kicks are likely to be blunted.

White Ladder ran only 7 days ago and Sean D Bowen takes over — track whether she travels with her usual fluency, as a quick turnaround on Good ground at Ayr over 6f is right in her wheelhouse if the pace is strong enough to close into.

Thunderstorm Katie has been placed in four of her last six but hasn't won since last year — monitor whether she travels with purpose in the first half of the race, as her record suggests she can hit the frame without necessarily breaking through.

runners_data.name: Braes Of Doune
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with genuine front-running credentials who goes on Good ground and has course form; Jim Goldie sends him out 24 days fresh with the tongue tie fitted, and his recent placed efforts over this trip suggest he can set a fair pace and make this competitive, though his OR of 57 limits ceiling.

runners_data.name: Millbuie
runners_data.note: Returned just eight days ago and shaped with some promise when third on Good ground last time; though he is a true hold-up horse by nature, the compressed field means he will likely be closer than ideal — his best turf form is on faster surfaces and stamina at a mile is untested over this sort of trip.

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: Decade-old gelding with consistent placed form on Good going, making his 15th Good-ground start with a respectable record; he naturally wants to come from behind but the single pace-setter here means he will not get the strong gallop he needs, and at OR 48 his margin for error is thin.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Four-year-old by Jason Hart who is, at heart, a hold-up performer, yet the single-pace-setter dynamic will push him closer to the early pace than he prefers; has two placed efforts on similar ground and steps up marginally in trip from his recent run, with the crossed noseband suggesting a free-going tendency.

runners_data.name: Thats My Boy Luke
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old has excellent Good-ground course-and-distance figures (13 from 15 sim-going runs, 2W6P) and wears a hood; David Allan takes the ride 22 days after his last start, and while he naturally settles toward the back, his record here is strong enough that he will be a danger if he can find a position closer to the pace than usual.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Pete
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler, 0 from 23 over the last 14 days, sends out a horse whose recent form reads 56-000 — three consecutive zeros tell a story of a horse who has gone cold; a natural closer in a race with a single controlled pace-setter is an awkward combination, and the 3lb claimer Alex Jary adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's five-year-old steps up from seven furlongs and all five recent runs have been at that trip or shorter on Good ground, so the extra furlong is a genuine unknown; the visor is fitted, the jockey is a 5lb apprentice, and a form string of 060807 provides no platform to expect improvement here.

runners_data.name: Eagles Dream
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's four-year-old has dropped sharply in trip — recent runs were over 9f-14f — and while he has shown ability at a mile earlier in his career, an OR of 64 and a recent last-of-eight effort leave questions about current form; his hold-up style suits nobody in this pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Starliner
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's five-year-old has a win and two places from six Good-ground runs over this exact trip, and his form figure of 1 on Good over a mile at his last visit to that combination stands out; Connor Beasley's experience is a plus and his Handicap mark of OR 63 is competitive, making him the horse whose style — prominent enough, resilient enough — best matches the race shape on offer.

races.paceDynamic: Braes Of Doune is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner handicap over Ayr's flat mile, and with no genuine challenger for the early lead, he is set to bowl along at a controlled, self-selected tempo under Paul Mulrennan — not a punishing gallop, but a steady, rhythmic pace that keeps the field compressed and denies closers a true test of stamina. The bulk of the field — Runninsonofagun, Whiskey Pete, Thats My Boy Luke, Millbuie and Golden Valour — are natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions on the map because the field cannot accommodate every closer at the rear; in reality, several of these will shuffle forward to fill the vacuum behind Braes Of Doune, meaning midfield will be tight and busy. This race shape — a single, uncontested pace-setter at a manageable gallop — classically favours horses who can travel prominently in his wake and pounce when the tempo stays honest, rather than deep closers needing a strong pace to pull them through. With so many genuine hold-up types unable to secure their natural position, the tactical advantage tilts firmly toward those who can sit second or third and strike from a handy berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Braes Of Doune Controls, Prominent Striker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Braes Of Doune leads unchallenged at a fair pace and a prominent-tracking runner has the quality to collar him in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Braes Of Doune sets an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race sets up as a procession until the field straightens; a horse travelling smoothly just off the leader's quarters has only to quicken past one rival rather than pick through traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Braes Of Doune Outstays Field, Makes All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains so controlled that the leader's energy reserves are intact entering the final furlong and no pursuer can sustain an effort.
scenarios.body: Braes Of Doune, never headed and never extended, simply gallops rivals into submission on honest Good ground; his course-and-distance form and proven ability to win from the front at this level give him a legitimate chance of holding on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo drops so sharply mid-race that the whole field bunches and the finish becomes a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace turns the race into a dash over the final quarter-mile, favouring the horse with the best finishing kick from a handy position; Starliner, who has won over this course and distance on Good ground, and Runninsonofagun, who has tactical speed, would be best placed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Braes Of Doune sets a surprisingly strong early gallop that strings out the field and exhausts the prominent runners, leaving a gap for genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because the pace evidence points to a controlled tempo, and the horses best-suited to a strong-pace-and-stay finish — Millbuie and Golden Valour — are older, lower-rated and have been inconsistent; even if the pace lifts, their recent form gives little confidence.

watchPoints.text: Starliner (Connor Beasley) has course-and-distance winning form on Good ground and is the horse most capable of sitting handily off Braes Of Doune's single controlled pace and striking — watch whether Beasley positions him second or third from the outset.

Braes Of Doune (Paul Mulrennan) is the only genuine front-runner and if he is allowed to set his own tempo unchallenged, he could dictate to a degree that makes him very hard to catch — monitor whether anything tries to press him early.

Runninsonofagun and Thats My Boy Luke are both natural hold-up horses likely to find themselves pushed closer than ideal as the field fills the vacuum behind the leader — watch for crowding and interference in the first two furlongs as multiple "closers" jostle for the same midfield positions.

Whiskey Pete's trainer Nigel Tinkler is 0 from 23 over the last 14 days — a cold trainer stat on a horse already showing three consecutive poor runs is a notable demerit in a race with little margin for error.

Eagles Dream has raced almost exclusively at 9f-14f recently and drops to 1m — watch whether he fails to settle or fades from two furlongs out, which would confirm the trip is sharper than he now wants.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo with solid recent form over this course and distance including two placings at 7f on Good, but a natural hold-up horse whose true home is at the rear; in a small field with a single pacemaker, finding clear daylight from off the pace will be harder than his map position suggests.

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Four-year-old trained by Gary Rutherford who has placed over this trip on Good ground before, though his record of 0 wins from 9 similar-going runs is a concern; genuine closer by inclination but the lack of strong pace to close into makes his preferred race shape unlikely to materialise today.

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's four-year-old has one win and three places from a similar-going sample but recent form figures show no consistency, and while he wants to race from off the pace, the compressed nature of this field in a slowly-run race means he may find rivals too close to pick off late.

runners_data.name: Ramon Di Loria
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner for Ewan Whillans, who has a runner in the last fortnight; his prominent tag here is slightly out of natural role as he leads rather than tracks, but his position is unchallenged and he can control the tempo — his consistency at this trip and on Good ground is the key positive.

runners_data.name: Tap Dancer
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old is stepping sharply back in trip having raced over 8–11f in recent starts, and Paul Mulrennan takes the ride; the distance drop and a hold-up style in a race where pace is limited are two compounding negatives that make his chance dependent on others going too fast early.

runners_data.name: Penny Mountain
runners_data.note: Jake Dickson claims 7lbs for Gary Rutherford's five-year-old, who has placed twice recently at sprint trips; a natural closer who has been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, meaning he will not get his usual ground and must quicken from closer than ideal.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' five-year-old carries the top weight of 140lbs and has a modest recent form string of 96-885; his hold-up style and step up from 5–6f to 7f today, combined with the absence of strong pace to close into, makes this a difficult ask even with Connor Beasley in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Jkr Cobbler
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's seven-year-old arrives with a recent 7f win on Good ground and a form figure of 1 in his latest start — the most relevant recent form in the race; racing prominently behind Ramon Di Loria is his natural role and he rates as the most likely beneficiary of a steady-tempo scenario where first run wins it.

runners_data.name: War Memorial
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney's five-year-old has two wins and three places from his five-run history sample, including two wins at 7f on Good ground; Conor Whiteley claims 5lbs and the horse's ability to finish strongly from a midfield position makes him a genuine player if the pace is steady enough to set up a strong final furlong.

races.paceDynamic: Ramon Di Loria is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no rival likely to press him hard from the outset over 7f on Good ground at Ayr, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a pressured burn. Jkr Cobbler is the one prominent type capable of tracking him from close range, meaning the tempo is unlikely to be truly test-setting — a pace that flatters those who can travel close to the front rather than those who need a strong gallop to close into. The field nominally shows several hold-up types in midfield, but Monhammer, Due Respect, Bantz, and Penny Mountain are all redistributed from a genuine hold-up position because there are more true closers than the map can place at the rear; they are unlikely to secure their natural ground in a small, slowly-run field. This race shape — a lone front-runner, a steady tempo, and a compressed field — firmly favours horses that can race prominently or at worst close to the pace, giving them first run and the ability to quicken off a comfortable gallop rather than needing a wall of pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria dictates an unchallenged, measured tempo and the race is decided by who can quicken soonest from a handy position.
scenarios.body: Ramon Di Loria sets a sustainable gallop that compresses the field, and Jkr Cobbler or War Memorial — both capable of racing prominently and finishing off — produce winning runs before the hold-up horses can close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely slow and the field concertinas, allowing the few true closers to benefit from a sprint finish in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A dawdle through the first half of the race turns the closing stages into a sprint, where horses with finishing pace rather than positional advantage thrive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria sets a pace that proves deceptively strong and the field misjudges, failing to close until too late.
scenarios.body: The lone front-runner steals enough of a break to maintain his advantage into the final furlong, with Jkr Cobbler the nearest pursuer but unable to reel him in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Wide Draw Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the start is muddled or multiple horses make unexpected moves for position, scrambling the anticipated race shape.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of several hold-up types into the midfield creates traffic issues and positional conflicts, handing the race to whichever horse avoids trouble and finds a clear run.

watchPoints.text: Jkr Cobbler is the standout positional threat — if he slots in smoothly behind Ramon Di Loria and gets first run into the final two furlongs, his recent 7f Good-ground win suggests he is the hardest to peg back.

Ramon Di Loria could steal this race if the jockeys on the hold-up horses misjudge the pace and allow him a soft lead that nobody challenges — watch whether anyone commits to tracking him from the outset.

War Memorial's two wins over 7f on Good ground make him a significant danger if he can secure a prominent enough position; Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim eases his weight and he should not be underestimated finishing from midfield.

Multiple redistributed hold-up types — Monhammer, Due Respect, Bantz, Penny Mountain — are all likely to crowd the midfield rather than settle at the rear, increasing the risk of traffic problems in the closing stages for any horse needing a clear run.

Tap Dancer's step back from 10f-plus trips to 7f for the first time in this campaign is a notable flag — if he fails to settle or finds the pace insufficient to close into, Paul Mulrennan may struggle to place him competitively from a hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6yo has won at 9f on Good ground and finished third over 10f recently, suggesting the 1m2f trip is within range; Paul Mulrennan retains the partnership, she goes in first-time hood (hg:p), and 16 days since last run looks fresh enough — the chief closer to Spiritoftheblues if the pace is on.

runners_data.name: Pol Roger
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this Michael Dods hold-up type who has placed twice at 10f on Good but has been below-par at 8f; stepping back to 10f on similar ground is positive, though a 24-day break and a tendency to find one or two too good means he needs everything to go right from the back.

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's 4yo has a progressive profile at staying trips and recorded a placing at 12f on Good, making the distance no concern; in truth a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is off the pace, though with so few runners he may find himself closer to the action than ideal — the STYLE_FIT tag tempers expectations if this race requires him to race prominently.

runners_data.name: Spiritoftheblues
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 3yo won over 7f on Good and finished second over 8f, so the step to 1m2f is an open question on stamina, but he is clearly the controlling pace influence here and Tudhope's ability to settle him in front at his own rhythm is the decisive tactical factor in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's lightly-raced 3yo has posted five consecutive placings without winning, all at shorter trips up to 8f, and the step to 10f is unproven; naturally a hold-up type who has been mapped forward by field composition rather than any inclination to race prominently, and 10 days since last run is a short turnaround — her finishing effort will depend heavily on the pace scenario unfolding in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: Spiritoftheblues is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and, with no rival willing or likely to challenge for the lead, Daniel Tudhope can dictate terms at a measured, controlled gallop over this 1m2f trip on Good ground at Ayr. The pace is unlikely to be fierce — one horse setting its own rhythm against hold-up rivals typically produces a steadier early tempo, which compresses the race into a late dash and rewards those with tactical speed rather than pure finishing reserves. Pearl Eye and Pol Roger are the principal closers, while Polygram and Light The Night Up are genuine hold-up types that have been mapped forward because the rear of the field is oversubscribed — neither is truly racing from their natural position, and that redistribution weakens the case for a truly strong late surge from the back. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or pace-setting profile: Spiritoftheblues controls the race from the front, and any horse capable of travelling just off that lone lead without cover — rather than trailing a length behind a slow-run bunch — holds a significant tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Spiritoftheblues bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair-but-sustainable tempo, allowing Tudhope to conserve energy and kick clear before rivals can close.
scenarios.body: Spiritoftheblues controls every yard, dictating the fractions to suit a horse that clearly relishes being on or near the pace; the hold-up brigade face a flat-run finish where the leader has already gone.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Leader In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fair enough to keep the race honest and Pearl Eye or Pol Roger travel powerfully through the contest to collar Spiritoftheblues late.
scenarios.body: A genuine Good-ground gallop over 1m2f can stretch the field enough for a hold-up horse making one sustained run; Pearl Eye's recent win at this trip and style of racing makes her the most credible closer in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Burn Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Spiritoftheblues is restrained or an unexpectedly crawling tempo bunches the field, turning the race into a sprint from 2f out.
scenarios.body: A muddling pace erases Spiritoftheblues's positional advantage and gifts a sharp-actioned runner that can quicken off a slow pace the winning opportunity; Light The Night Up's compact form profile suggests some ability to quicken, though she is racing out of her natural hold-up role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types — Polygram or Light The Night Up — manages to find a seam of daylight and produce an unexpected late burst.
scenarios.body: Both horses are true hold-up types shuffled forward on the map due to field composition, so their true style is compromised here; however, a collapse in the front-runners would open a late-run window that could flatter either at big odds.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Spiritoftheblues jumps cleanly and immediately establishes the lead — if Tudhope is slow away and another runner challenges for the front early, the entire pace dynamic shifts and the race shape becomes unpredictable.

Pearl Eye is the horse most likely to challenge the leader in the straight; if she travels smoothly in second and Mulrennan produces her with a well-timed run, she represents the biggest danger to Spiritoftheblues dictating on his own terms.

The stamina of Spiritoftheblues over 1m2f is untested — all form is at 7f-8f — and if he weakens inside the final furlong having led throughout, the race could be thrown open to the closers in a manner the pace map does not fully anticipate.

Polygram and Light The Night Up are both natural hold-up types squeezed into midfield positions by field composition; if neither can settle into their preferred rhythm off a slow pace, their effectiveness late in the race is materially reduced regardless of their handicap marks.

The Good ground is confirmed consistent across all races on the card at Ayr today, removing any going variance as a factor — all horses are operating on a reliable surface and recent Good-ground form is directly applicable.

runners_data.name: Inappropriate
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who ran second over 17f on good ground 19 days ago, showing stamina is not in doubt; wearing a hood and a tongue-tie, she will need the pace to be strong enough to reel in the principals from the rear, which is far from guaranteed here.

runners_data.name: Simply Ruby
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner dropping back from a 292-day absence, she showed pace over 12f on good and soft ground but steps up markedly in trip; Ed Walker's yard has good recent strike rate and the uncontested lead here is a significant tactical asset, though fitness after a long layoff is the key question.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: A genuine stayer with two wins on good going over 16f, Dianne Sayer's veteran has course-relevant credentials at this trip; Molly Gunn takes over in the saddle and the consistent hitting of the frame on similar ground (5P from 12 runs) marks Simple Star as a durable each-way type, even if a win has proved elusive lately.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's horse has won twice recently including over 15f on good ground, and his last four runs show a pattern of placing or winning in this distance band; he is a natural hold-up horse by inclination but with several similar types in the field, he is unlikely to be as far back as he'd prefer, which could actually suit if the pace is moderate.

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in fine heart with three places from his last four runs, two of which were wins, and he handles good ground well over distances up to 14f; Oliver Carmichael's booking is a positive for Jim Goldie's second string, though the step up to 13f-plus tested him before and 1m5f is a fresh stamina question.

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran who is a natural hold-up type, Shay Farmer's mount has been running over shorter trips recently (9–10f) and the 1m5f distance looks a stretch on that recent evidence; with STYLE_FIT flagged and limited recent form over this sort of trip, there are significant doubts about him getting a truly favourable position in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Simply Ruby is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners over 1m5f on good ground at Ayr, she is likely to bowl along at a controlled, uncontested tempo that suits her perfectly. Annandale will press from a prominent position and may apply some mid-race pressure, but with no genuine pace rival to force the issue early, the overall gallop should remain measured and sustainable. The field contains more natural hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the back — Cascade Hall and Glasses Up are both true hold-up horses but are mapped to midfield because that space is already crowded, meaning neither is likely to be in their natural position. A steady, front-runner-dictated tempo over this staying trip on a flat track with no genuine pace battle heavily favours horses who can travel prominently or press the leader, rather than those trying to close from off the pace on a soft, uneventful gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Simply Ruby dictates a measured, uncontested gallop and the field fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Simply Ruby leads throughout at a sustainable pace that suits her stamina profile, with the race never truly tested until late; Annandale, pressing from just off the leader, is ideally placed to pounce if the leader tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If Annandale pushes the tempo and forces Simply Ruby into a genuine duel from halfway.
scenarios.body: The increased pace suits a horse with tactical versatility and a strong finishing effort over this trip; Annandale's good recent form over similar distances on good ground makes her the most likely beneficiary if the race develops into a true test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to stop the leaders and a hold-up horse finds clear running in the straight.
scenarios.body: Inappropriate has course-relevant form at this sort of trip and ran second over 17f on good ground recently, making her the most credible closer; Simple Star's two wins on similar going at 16f also give her a legitimate claim if the pace collapses the front two.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically and an unexposed or lightly-raced runner benefits from chaos or a career-best effort.
scenarios.body: Cascade Hall has won twice in this distance band on good ground and is on a retrieval run after a quick turnaround, giving Jim Goldie's yard a live contender if the race shape happens to play into her natural rhythm.

watchPoints.text: Simply Ruby's fitness after 292 days off is the single biggest race-shaper — if she blows up before the turn-in, the entire race dynamic inverts and hold-up horses gain ground they would not otherwise see.

Cascade Hall and Glasses Up are both natural hold-up types who cannot all settle at the back in a six-runner field; watch the early stages to see if either is pushed wider or higher than they want, which would compromise their chance significantly.

Annandale ran just seven days ago and is on a quick turnaround — Jim Goldie runs two in this race and if Annandale shows any sign of tiredness from that effort, Cascade Hall's fresher legs could switch the yard's best hope.

With only six runners and a flat Ayr straight, draw and positioning out of the gate matter more than usual — a clean break for Simply Ruby effectively seals the pace scenario before a single furlong has been run.
